original_question: Let E be the extraspecial p-group p^(1+2)_+ of order p^3 and exponent p for an odd prime p. A graph in Theorem 6.2 of the cited companion paper describes the stable splitting of B G for all p-local finite groups G having Sylow p-subgroup E when p = 3. Determine the analogous stable-splitting graph for p = 7, using Theorem 9.4 from the same paper as a partial input.
target_in_paper: Section 6, “The problem presented by Nobuaki Yagita”: write down, for p = 7, the graph analogous to Theorem 6.2 of Yagita’s companion paper that encodes the stable splitting of BG for groups/p-local finite groups over E = p_+^{1+2}; the problem statement explicitly says that Theorem 9.4 of the companion paper gives only a partial result. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the extraspecial group E = p_+^{1+2}, the role of Theorem 6.2 as the p = 3 model graph, and the fact that the p = 7 question is to go beyond the partial decompositions already recorded in Theorem 9.4. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
missing_details: The paper’s natural scope is p-local finite groups over E, not only finite groups with Sylow p-subgroup E; for finite groups BG is the p-completed classifying space, while for a p-local finite group ⟨E, F, L⟩ its classifying space is |L|^_p. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-019s.pdf))

To be stand-alone, the question should specify what the “graph” means in this paper: in Theorem 6.2 and Theorem 9.4, a label X1 ... Xs G means BG ≃ X1 ∨ ··· ∨ Xs. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-019s.pdf))

The standard stable summands should be named explicitly: the decompositions are written in terms of X_{q,k}, L(2,k), and L(1,k), and the paper also uses M(2) = L(2,0) ∨ L(1,0). ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-019s.pdf))

The p = 7 problem is meant to range over the full Ruiz–Viruel 7-local classification relevant here, including the sporadic cases He, He:2, Fi24', Fi24, O'N, O'N:2 and the three exotic 7-local finite groups RV1, RV2, RV3; Theorem 9.4 covers only part of that full graph. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-019s.pdf))

Your wording turns Theorem 9.4 into a method instruction (“using Theorem 9.4 as a partial input”), whereas the original problem only states that Theorem 9.4 is a partial result; the faithful formulation should ask for completion of that partial graph. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))

If “analogous graph” is meant literally, the question should ask for the complete p = 7 analogue of Theorem 6.2, not just isolated stable decompositions for selected groups. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-019s.pdf))

The vertex set is still implicit in your draft: the p = 3 model graph in Theorem 6.2 includes both sporadic groups and extension groups E⋊H, so the p = 7 analogue should similarly clarify whether all relevant extension cases E⋊H from the 7-local classification are to be included. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-019s.pdf))
refined_question: Let E = 7_+^{1+2} be the extraspecial group of order 7^3 and exponent 7, and let BG denote the p-completed classifying space of a finite group with Sylow 7-subgroup E, or more generally the classifying space of a 7-local finite group over E. Determine the complete p = 7 analogue of Theorem 6.2 in Yagita’s companion paper: for every 7-local finite group over E occurring in the Ruiz–Viruel classification, write the full stable wedge decomposition of BG into the standard indecomposable summands X_{q,k}, L(2,k), and L(1,k) (with M(2) = L(2,0) ∨ L(1,0)), and arrange these decompositions in a graph in the same sense as Theorem 6.2, namely so that a label X1 ... Xs G records a stable equivalence BG ≃ X1 ∨ ··· ∨ Xs. In particular, extend the partial p = 7 graph given in Theorem 9.4 to a complete graph. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-019s.pdf))
justification: This is the narrowest paper-faithful reformulation because the problem-session note asks exactly for the p = 7 counterpart of the p = 3 graph from Theorem 6.2 and explicitly points to Theorem 9.4 only as a partial result. The companion paper supplies the hidden context your draft leaves implicit: what BG means, that the stable-splitting theorem is being applied to p-local finite groups over E as well as finite groups, how the summands X_{q,k}, L(2,k), L(1,k) are defined, and which p = 7 cases belong to the classification. Hence the sharp stand-alone question is to complete the full p = 7 stable-splitting graph, not merely to compute one more example. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
